_about: The towns of the Lakes frontier in 1811 (design doc 6.1), read by tools/world/place_towns.py, which lays each one out on dry ground near its real place and writes its people into the scene as NpcSpawn markers (Cast/Towns). Populations are the town proper about 1811-12; the garrisons are peacetime strength before the war. 'farm' is the share of the town's families who farm (the habitants' ribbon farms of Detroit and the Essex shore, the loyalists' park lots at York and Niagara); the rest are tradesmen, labourers, carters and boatmen. 'names' picks the surname pool; 'french' is the share of French-Canadian families. 'notables' are people known to have lived there then; everyone else is generated. 'lay' is the order the towns take their ground in, where two want the same shore. 'at' is a cell to build round instead of the real place, where that lies inside a bigger neighbour at the map's scale ('at_why' says so).

towns.name: Detroit
towns.note: The old French town on the strait, rebuilt on Judge Woodward's plan after the fire of 1805: the capital of Michigan Territory, a town of habitants, Scots and Yankee merchants, the first fur market below Michilimackinac.

towns.name: Amherstburg
towns.note: The King's town at the mouth of the Detroit River, built when the British gave up Detroit in 1796: the Provincial Marine's dockyard, the Indian Department's storehouse, where the western nations come each year for the King's presents.

towns.name: York
towns.note: Governor Simcoe's capital of Upper Canada on Toronto Bay: the Parliament buildings, St. James's, a few streets of frame houses and the garrison at the mouth of the Humber road.

towns.name: Niagara
towns.note: Newark, the old capital at the mouth of the Niagara: Butler's Rangers' town, St. Mark's, the court house and Navy Hall, and Fort George on the common, looking across the river at the Americans in Fort Niagara.

towns.name: Queenston
towns.note: The landing at the foot of the Niagara escarpment, where the portage road round the falls begins: Robert Hamilton's warehouses and wharf, and a village of loyalist families.
towns.at_why: Queenston is eleven kilometres up the river from Niagara, which at the map's scale is inside Niagara's own streets: it is built on the next free ground up the shore.

towns.name: Fort Niagara
towns.note: The old French stone fort on the American side of the Niagara's mouth, given up by the British in 1796: a garrison of the United States Artillery, a sutler and the officers' families.
